follower_mon_sprite_rendering.recipe: species = from GetFollowerMon logic (see follower_recipe), NOT from the object struct. info = 0x0888C430 + species*36 (ARRAY of ObjectEventGraphicsInfo structs, NOT pointers; species = internal id, 412 entries). Frame sheet: images ptr @info+0x1C -> first SpriteFrameImage entry's dataPtr = LZ77-COMPRESSED blob (GBA BIOS LZ77, 0x10 header) decompressing to 0xC00 = 6 frames x 0x200 (32x32 4bpp); frames are stand/walk PAIRS per direction: 0=stand South, 1=walk South, 2=stand North, 3=walk North, 4=stand West, 5=walk West (East = frame 4 h-flipped). CORRECTED 2026-08-19 -- this entry previously claimed 0/1/2 = stand S/N/W, which is the NPC/player order and is WRONG for mon sheets; it made a follower facing north render facing south and one facing west render facing north. Both the JS and Python renderers took the mapping from this line, so they agreed byte-for-byte while both were wrong -- cross-implementation agreement proves consistency, not correctness. Established by rendering all six frames of two species and looking at them. Palette: LZ77 blob at [0x08751738 + species*8] (species-indexed {u32 lzPalPtr, u32 tag} table, decompresses to 32 bytes = 16 x BGR555, color 0 transparent)

badge_pixel_art.recipe: LZ77-decompress the sheet at 0x08A60760 (GBA BIOS LZ77, header 10 00 04 00) -> 0x400 bytes = 32 tiles of 4bpp = a 128x16px image, 8 badges of 16x16 left-to-right (Boulder..Earth). Badge i (0-based) = tiles {2i, 2i+1, 16+2i, 16+2i+1} (top-left, top-right, bottom-left, bottom-right; standard GBA 4bpp 8x8 tiles, low nibble = left pixel). map_rendering.blockdata: u16 per map cell (row-major, width*height): bits 0-9 metatileId, bits 10-11 collision (0 = passable), bits 12-15 elevation
map_rendering.metatile: THREE-LAYER (the known 3-layer-metatiles patch): 12 x u16 = 24-byte stride - bottom layer quads TL,TR,BL,BR, then middle, then top. Entry: bits 0-9 tileId (<640 primary tiles, >=640 secondary at tileId-640), 0x400 hflip, 0x800 vflip, bits 12-15 palette (0-12). Composite bottom->middle->top with color 0 transparent on the upper layers (porymap-style; matches live captures pixel-structurally per parser-builder's 83.5% transition test and my corrected render). (Earlier 8xu16/16-byte claim RETRACTED; a 24-byte ldmia/stmia metatile copy also exists @0x0816364A)
map_rendering.palettes_note: ROM palettes are the DAY colors; the game applies day/night tinting at runtime from the accelerated clock (the live capture at in-game 21:16 shows all palettes darkened ~45%). Render with raw ROM palettes for a daytime map, or scale for night flavor
map_rendering.verified: rasterized the 15x10 patch around the player's real position and matched it to the live overworld screenshot (research/dumps/trainer-card/menu-open/screen.png); validation render saved as research/dumps/trainer-card/celadon-render-validation.png

day_night_tint.driver: DNS driver fn @0x08141B00: runs the clock update (0x081A02F4), then unless the override byte @EWRAM 0x020377D3 is set (1..0x1A -> forced mode-1), reads hour (SB2+0xF5E) and minute (SB2+0xF5F) and dispatches hour through a 26-entry handler table @ROM 0x0894EFB0 (entries 24/25 = special modes; override 0xD9 = freeze). Handlers write the tint state to IWRAM 0x3000B36 (mode byte: 0=night-ish,1=?,2=day/clear) and 0x3000B38 {u32 currentTint, u32 targetTint, u32 weights} which the palette-commit path (unfaded 0x020377F0 -> faded 0x02037BF0, blend fn 0x08146584, per-palette exemption masks) applies every refresh

schedule.04:00-06:59: dawn ramp: word0 (night) -> word1 (twilight), minute-interpolated across the 3h window

tint_words.note: packed {coeff,color} format only partially decoded - use the measured approximation below for rendering

day_night_tint.measured_approximation: live capture at in-game 21:16 (63% through the evening ramp): all overworld palettes multiplied per-channel by approximately R x0.61, G x0.53, B x0.61 (slightly blue-purple night). Full night is modestly stronger; for the page a single 'night' filter of ~(0.55, 0.48, 0.55) with a slight blue push looks right
day_night_tint.chip_rule: for a DAY/NIGHT chip: NIGHT = hours 20-23 and 0-6 (tinted), DAY = 7-19 (clear or nearly so); the old 6-18 guess was wrong - full day starts at 10:00 and dimming starts at 18:00
day_night_tint.interiors: the override byte is cleared on every map load and a mapType check (header +0x17) at 0x08140E60 gates the system; indoor map types appear to skip tinting (the exemption also runs through per-palette masks in the commit path). Medium confidence on the exact indoor rule
day_night_tint.confidence: high (schedule/table/constants disassembled; tint magnitude live-measured), medium (packed-word semantics, interior rule)

rom_functions.note: Named ROM code addresses, each identified by disassembling this ROM (research/tools/disasm.py) and matching the instruction sequence against the pokeemerald source that produced it. Thumb entry points; call them with |1. Established while proving out the bag/sell path - see the 'Task data, and the bag sell path' section of hack-offsets.md

ResetTasks.note: loops 16 tasks at stride 0x28 from gTasks (0x03005BB8): func=TaskDummy, isActive=0, prev=i, next=i+1, priority=0xFF, memset(data,0,0x20). Independently re-confirms the gTasks base and the 40-byte Task stride

CreateTask.note: scans gTasks[i].isActive (0x03005BBC = gTasks+4) from i=0 upward and takes the FIRST free slot -> the first CreateTask after ResetTasks always returns task id 0

TaskDummy.note: the no-op task func ResetTasks installs; seen as 0x081B9741 in every free slot of a live gTasks dump

AddMoney.note: called as AddMoney(&SaveBlock1->money, amount); callers build the pointer as *(gSaveBlock1Ptr) + 0x29C (emitted as movs #0xA7 / lsls #2), which re-confirms the money offset

RemoveBagItem.note: RemoveBagItem(itemId, count); returns FALSE and removes NOTHING when count exceeds the amount held

CreateBagInputHandlerTask.note: SetupBagMenu state 14; the first CreateTask after that ResetTasks, so the bag's input task is ALWAYS task id 0 -> its data[] lives at 0x03005BC0..0x03005BE5

DisplaySellItemPriceAndConfirm.note: quotes (GetItemPrice(item)/2) * tItemCount via 'I can pay Y{STR_VAR_1}.'; reads tItemCount as ldrsh [gTasks+8 + 40*taskId, #0x10]

ConfirmSell.note: same price math behind 'Turned over the {STR_VAR_2} and received Y{STR_VAR_1}.'; note the hack converts with 7 digits where vanilla passes 6, matching its uncapped money

SellItem.note: RemoveBagItem(item, tItemCount) then AddMoney(&money, (GetItemPrice(item)/2) * tItemCount) - the AddMoney runs whatever RemoveBagItem returned

PokedexSearch_task.note: unrelated subsystem that also uses task data[8] ('Searching...' / 'No matching Pokemon were found.'); recorded because it owns the only absolute literal to gTasks+0x18 in the ROM and is easy to mistake for the bag code

gSpecialVar_ItemId.note: the item the bag/shop flow is acting on; read by the sell path immediately before CopyItemName/GetItemPrice
